# 1 Enoch Chapter 60 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 60:7-8 — Leviathan (female) and Behemoth (male) — gender assignment

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-female-monster named Leviathan ... the-male is-named Behemoth" | Literal; Ge'ez assigns explicit gender |
| LOGOS | "a female monster named Leviathan ... the male is named Behemoth" | Preserves gender assignment |
| PNEUMA | "a female creature called Leviathan ... a male creature called Behemoth" | 'Creature' preferred over 'monster' |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Key decision: retain 'monster' (EMET/LOGOS) vs. 'creature' (PNEUMA). Adopted 'monster' — the Ge'ez term implies something monstrous and fearful, not merely 'creature.' The gender assignment (female/male) is preserved by all three translators and is significant — this is the Enochic expansion of Job 40–41, which does not specify gender.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS on 'monster.' Gender assignment: full convergence.

---

## 60:8 — 'Duidain' — the location of Behemoth

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Duidain" | Preserved as a proper name |
| LOGOS | "Duidain" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "Duidain" | Agrees; notes it may reflect a geographical memory |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Full convergence. 'Duidain' preserved untranslated as the Ge'ez proper name. Attempts to identify it with 'Nod' (east of Eden, Gen 4:16) or with the Dead Sea region are speculative.

**Status:** Full convergence.

---

## 60:10 — 'son of man' as address to Enoch

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Thou-son of-man" | Preserved literally; the Ge'ez walda sab' = son of man |
| LOGOS | "You, son of man" | Preserves the address; theologically significant |
| PNEUMA | "You, son of man" | Agrees; notes the echo of ch. 46 and 71 |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Full convergence. 'Son of man' is preserved as a formal address to Enoch by the angel — this is significant because Enoch himself will be identified as the Son of Man in 71:14. The address here (from an angel to Enoch) carries that anticipation.

**Status:** Full convergence. Theologically significant term.

---

## 60:14 — thunder and lightning as 'inseparable yet not one'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-both-go-together through-the-spirit and-separate-not" | Literal; the Ge'ez spirit/wind (manfas) mediates |
| LOGOS | "they both go together through the spirit and do not separate" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "they travel together through the spirit and never part" | 'Never part' slightly more emphatic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The philosophical point — two distinct things unified through a third mediating spirit — is preserved in all three versions. LOGOS's rendering is most precise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 60:25 — fragmentary ending

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "These-two-monsters ... shall-feed..." | Preserves the fragment as-is |
| LOGOS | "These two monsters ... shall feed..." | Agrees — fragment preserved |
| PNEUMA | "These two creatures ... shall feed..." | Same |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three translators agree to preserve the fragment without expansion. The ending is incomplete in all Ge'ez MSS. Some scholars reconstruct 'shall feed' as referring to the eschatological banquet for the righteous (cf. 2 Bar 29:4), but this should not be inserted into the text.

**Status:** Full convergence. Fragment preserved as-is.

---
